title: Plasma Lithography Surface Patterning for Creation of Cell Networks
protocol: Create molds used for patterning cell networks.
Design patterns using CAD software to guide cell adhesion and placement.
Send designed patterns to a company for photomask production.
Pattern glass slides with thin positive or thick negative resists using photolithography.
Attach patterned slide to a stack of unpatterned slides in a clean flow hood.
Prepare a container of tinfoil larger than the stack of slides.
Pour 30 g of Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) over the photolithographically patterned surface.
Degass the PDMS and allow it to cure for one to two days.
Peel PDMS off the master pattern to form a mold.
Mix 6 g of 2-part epoxy for 1 minute.
Pour the mixed epoxy into the PDMS mold and degas quickly.
Allow the epoxy to partially cure for one hour.
Add more epoxy on top without degassing to produce a thicker structure.
Allow the epoxy to cure completely for one to two days.
Remove the cured epoxy from the PDMS master mold.
Wrap tape around the epoxy mold to form a container.
Pour PDMS onto the epoxy mold and degas the PDMS.
Allow the PDMS to cure completely for one to two days.
Peel the cured PDMS off the epoxy mold and store it to maintain cleanliness.
Cut small sections of the working PDMS mold.
Place the sections onto a polystyrene Petri dish.
Label the locations of these mold sections on the dish.
Form a tripod from the small sections and weight them for conformal contact with the dish surface.
Place the assembly into the plasma chamber.
Initiate plasma treatment at 150 Pa and 29.6 W (maximum power) for 10 minutes using air plasma.
Remove the mold and weight arrangement after plasma treatment.
Place the Petri dish under UV light for 10 minutes of sterilization inside the biosafety cabinet.
Store the Petri dish in the biosafety cabinet until seeding with cells.
Cultivate SH-SY5Y CRL-2266 Human Neuroblastoma or other cells using standard protocols specific to each cell type.
Measure the confluence of SH-SHY5Y CRL-2266 Human Neuroblastoma cells visually before seeding onto the patterned surface.
Carry out standard cell splitting to remove cells from their Petri dish.
Dilute the free-floating cells to achieve the desired confluence on the patterned surface.
Seed the diluted cells onto the surface of the patterned Petri dish.
Allow the seeded cells to settle and attach to the surface.
Incubate the patterned Petri dish for several hours to several days while cells assemble onto the pattern.
Add retinoic acid (10 μM) daily in the dark to induce differentiation into neuron-like state.
Continue adding retinoic acid daily for several days until observable differentiation occurs.
Replace media every 3-4 days during culturing.
Take periodic images or videos of live cells to observe behavior over time.
Place cells in a microscope stage top incubator set at 37 °C, 100% humidity, and 5% CO2 for imaging.
Fix and stain the cells if observation under fluorescence is required.
Import captured images or videos into an image analysis system.
Measure growth rate of cells using the imported data.
Determine cell size through measurements in the image analysis system.
Calculate migration speed based on observations from images or videos.
Assess differentiation levels by analyzing images or videos.
Evaluate alignment of cells using image analysis tools.
Identify location of specific proteins within cells.
